# Steering wheel replacement and airbag swap

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Disconnect battery, remove old wheel with puller, swap in new one, then reconnect all wiring harnesses. [t1850]

## Tools

- Socket wrench [t1850]
- 10mm socket [t1850]
- 13mm socket [t1850]
- 16mm socket [t1850]
- 19mm socket [t1850]
- Phillips head screwdriver [t1850]
- Small flathead screwdriver [t1850]
- Steering wheel puller [t1850]

## Parts

- [Partial] Airbag assembly, if swapping [t1850]
- Cruise control buttons and cover [t1850]
- Leather steering wheel [t1850]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use an electric impact wrench instead of a regular socket for easier removal of the 19mm nut. [t1850]
- Align the vertical slit on the shaft with the round dimple mark on the wheel to ensure proper top-center positioning. [t1850]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Working directly in front of the airbag before disconnecting it, risking injury from the pyrotechnic charge. [t1850]
- [Partial] Dropping the disconnected airbag and triggering an accidental deployment. [t1850]
- Snagging the clock spring wires during removal or installation. [t1850]
